page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-88 is a compute-focused instance type within the C3 machine series. It is powered by a dedicated 4th Generation Intel Xeon Platinum 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, delivering 88 vCPUs across 44 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance features 176.0 GB of system memory, matching a compute-optimized 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 48 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache. The CPU features full support for modern instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (Tile and INT8), VAES, and SHA extensions. There are zero dedicated GPUs, and bundled local storage is listed as None, necessitating persistent network-attached storage disks.

Benchmark evaluations indicate excellent parallel processing and memory throughput characteristics. In multi-core tests, the c3-highcpu-88 achieves top-quartile performance, scoring 73,301.13 in stress-ng and 18,513.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Single-core performance falls in the average tier across metrics, registering 1,624.58 in stress-ng and 1,730.0 in Geekbench. Large uncached read bandwidth reaches 230.41 GB/sec, while write bandwidth measures 95.14 GB/sec. Specialized test suites demonstrate top 10% performance in Geekbench image processing (18,780.0) alongside top-quartile marks in software compilation with Clang (51,203.0), ray tracing (81,792.0), PassMark CPU encryption (76,839.22), and Redis SET operations (85.52 million ops/sec). The presence of Intel AMX extensions enables competitive CPU-bound LLM prompt processing speeds, reaching 2,854.67 tokens/sec on 135M parameter models.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the c3-highcpu-88 centers around dense parallel compute tasks where high memory capacity is not strictly required. Because memory capacity is bounded at 2 GB per thread, applications demanding significant memory-to-core footprints will encounter overhead, whereas thread-scalable CPU workloads leverage the high physical core count effectively. This instance type is ideally matched for continuous integration build clusters, parallel software compilation, scientific simulation, web serving tiers, and vector-accelerated inference tasks.
